features.name: Hall Monitoring Game
features.description: Team-based points system for hallway behavior and attendance with positive reinforcement
features.valueProposition: Reduces hallway issues, improves attendance, builds team spirit
keyPoints: Divide school into teams (by hallway or time block)
Award daily points to teams with best performance
Monthly rewards for winning teams (cookies, ice cream)
Visual reminders with posters and whiteboards
implementation: Points system for proper hall pass usage
Security officers distribute points for compliance
Negative points system (not below zero) for violations
Baseline points per day to avoid adversarial dynamics
risks: May need temporary implementation to establish norms

Hall passes can cost coins or currency
GPS tracking for pass usage verification (optional)

risks: Phone use in classroom concern - mitigate with iPad/public device

features.name: Cross-Domain Favorites
features.description: A consistent Favorites system for quickly pinning and reusing Keypad actions, symbols, spells, minimap tiles, and other eligible items across domains.
features.valueProposition: Reduce repeated navigation and make each user's most useful tools immediately available without fragmenting state between domains.
keyPoints: One Favorites model shared by Keypad and MINIMAP surfaces
Keypad support for Actions, Symbols, and Spells with predictable ordering
Minimap support for Tiles, including cross-domain tile references
Fast add, remove, reorder, and keyboard/controller-accessible retrieval
Per-user persistence with graceful offline behavior and conflict resolution
Eligibility, visibility, and permission checks before an item is shown or launched
Usage telemetry that measures successful retrieval without storing sensitive payloads
features: Favorite and unfavorite from item context menus, detail views, and the active Keypad/Minimap surface
Dedicated Favorites grouping with type labels, icons, stable names, and domain context
Drag-and-drop plus accessible move controls for custom ordering
Optional recents and most-used ranking kept separate from the user's pinned order
Duplicate prevention based on canonical item identity rather than display name
Stale-item treatment that preserves the entry while clearly explaining unavailable or moved content
Import and export of a versioned Favorites set for migration and recovery
implementation: Define a versioned FavoriteReference contract with canonical id, item type, domain, label snapshot, icon reference, source route, permissions metadata, createdAt, updatedAt, and sort order
Expose a shared favorites provider and reducer so Keypad and MINIMAP consume the same actions and selectors
Keep pinned order authoritative; calculate recents and usage ranking as separate derived views
Persist changes optimistically, queue offline mutations, and reconcile server conflicts with deterministic last-write handling plus order normalization
Resolve references through domain registries at render and launch time so renamed, deleted, or unauthorized items cannot silently execute
Use an explicit schema version and migration pipeline before accepting imported or persisted data
Instrument add, remove, reorder, open, unavailable, and permission-denied events with anonymized item type and domain only
requirements: A favorite can be launched in one interaction from its owning surface
The same favorite resolves to the same canonical item from Keypad, MINIMAP, and any future eligible surface
Favorites remain stable across reloads, account sessions, and supported devices
Unauthorized or unavailable items are never executable from Favorites
All actions are usable with keyboard navigation, screen readers, and touch/controller input
The UI remains responsive while persistence, reference resolution, or synchronization is pending
The feature has unit, integration, accessibility, and end-to-end coverage for happy, stale, offline, and conflict states
concerns: Cross-domain identity and permission rules must be settled before clients create references
Favorites should not become a second navigation hierarchy or obscure the full Keypad and Minimap inventories
Custom ordering must remain understandable when recents or recommendations are available
Label and icon snapshots need refresh rules so stale metadata does not mislead users
risks: Inconsistent canonical ids could create duplicates or launch the wrong item
Offline conflict handling could reorder or remove favorites unexpectedly
Large collections could degrade search, rendering, or synchronization performance
Telemetry could expose sensitive domain context if event fields are not constrained
examples: Pin a frequently used Action, Symbol, or Spell from the Keypad and launch it from the Favorites group
Pin a Tile in MINIMAP and retrieve that same Tile reference after switching domains
Open a stale favorite to see its last known label, current availability, and a route to find the replacement

features.name: Keypad Feedback Input & Output Tiles
features.description: Optional feedback controls that place one semi-transparent diamond tile on each side of the Symbol Grid keypad for tuning and displaying input/output performance.
features.valueProposition: Make keypad performance legible at a glance while giving users precise control over how accuracy, quality, speed, and time feedback is interpreted.
keyPoints: Add one Features toggle to enable or disable the paired Feedback Input and Feedback Output tiles
Place one diamond-shaped tile on each side of the keypad with consistent spacing, a modern border, and a connecting line
Keep the tiles semi-transparent and visually subordinate to the keypad while preserving clear state and focus affordances
Use four rarity/quality-mapped colors, with the canonical color and threshold values defined in the legend rather than duplicated in the tiles
Show an APM-style segmented bar display in the legend for each metric, adapted from the 4eye AI chat legend treatment
Support keyboard, pointer, touch, and screen-reader access without changing keypad geometry when the feature is off

autoOption.name: Auto
autoOption.description: Adapts to the active context and current keypad state

legend.display: APM-style segmented bars with the metric name, selected option, mapped rarity/quality color, actual threshold/value, and Auto state
legend.sourceOfTruth: The legend owns the option values, thresholds, rarity/quality colors, and bar labels; tiles consume the resolved legend state

settings.maxPreset: Set Accuracy, Quality, Speed, and Time to level 4 simultaneously

implementation: Define a shared feedback configuration contract for enabled state, metric selections, resolved values, rarity/quality mapping, and legend display data
Render the input tile before the keypad and the output tile after the keypad so both remain anchored to the keypad surface across responsive layouts
Use the existing Preferences control patterns for the toggle and five-option selectors, with Auto first or clearly marked as the default
Keep Auto white in the legend and do not assign it a rarity tier; resolve its live value before rendering the metric bar
Persist the setting per user and provide migration defaults for existing keypad preferences
Expose the All Settings Max preset as one action while retaining independent metric controls
requirements: When disabled, neither tile nor its connector occupies layout space
When enabled, exactly one input tile and one output tile are rendered on opposite sides of the keypad
Each metric offers exactly four named levels plus Auto, with Auto selected by default
The four level values and colors are defined once in the legend and remain synchronized with tile state
The All Settings Max preset resolves every metric to level 4
Legend bars expose actual values and labels rather than color-only meaning
All settings remain usable with keyboard navigation, assistive technology, touch, and reduced-motion preferences
concerns: Thresholds must be defined with product and gameplay owners before visual polish is finalized
The side tiles need a narrow-screen fallback that preserves keypad usability without overlap
Color mapping must retain readable contrast against semi-transparent surfaces and remain understandable without color
